name: Ossian Sorrel-Ginger Ale
description: A bold, deeply red craft-style ginger ale that replaces the standard ginger-ale profile with a base of real sorrel (dried hibiscus-adjacent, tart and floral) and fiery ginger root extract. Sharp, complex, and slightly intimidating to first-time drinkers.
flavor_profile: Aggressively tart sorrel, burning ginger heat, underlying earthy sweetness from raw cane, very dry finish — closer to a botanical tonic than a conventional sweet soda
cultural_context: Ossian Sorrel-Ginger has a devoted following among people who find most sodas cloying — it's the drink of bartenders, cooks, and anyone who considers themselves a flavor pragmatist. It's used as a mixer as often as a standalone drink. In Shelf bars, it gets cut with cheap synth-rum. In Tier 3 cocktail lounges, it sits next to artisanal spirits at three times the price.
story_hooks: Ossian's ginger root supply comes from a single vertical farm cooperative in the Milwaukee sector — the cooperative is about to be bought out by a corponation, and Ossian's founder is trying to raise enough capital to buy it themselves before the deal closes.

Someone has been using Ossian bottles to transport a controlled BCI-enhancement compound — the bottles look identical to legitimate product, and Ossian is facing legal exposure for something they had nothing to do with.

A food historian has published research suggesting the Ossian recipe is nearly identical to a traditional Caribbean sorrel drink from the early 21st century — the family that originally held that recipe wants recognition, and the story is more complicated than either side wants to admit.
